_what: Single source of truth for the SV Zero profile pack. tools/generate.py emits SuperSlicer and PrusaSlicer bundles and OrcaSlicer profiles from this, so the three cannot drift the way the hand-maintained SS and PS bundles already did.

machine.name: SV Zero
machine._max_volumetric_note: Sovol's published rating, 85W/24V ceramic hotend. Emitted into *SV Zero General* as `max_volumetric_speed`, which in PrusaSlicer/SuperSlicer is the HOTEND capability limit (Print settings -> Speed). The material limit is filament_max_volumetric_speed. Per Prusa's docs the effective cap is the LOWER of the two, so machine and material stay separable and no tier needs hand-capping. Orca has no process-level equivalent -- only the filament one -- so for Orca the machine ceiling has to be folded into each filament profile.

limits._what: Stock Sovol Zero motion limits, from printer.cfg [printer].
limits._why: Klipper's SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT does not clamp. toolhead.py assigns self.max_accel = max_accel outright, so a sliced file asking ACCEL=40000 RAISES a machine whose config says 5000. A max_accel in printer.cfg is therefore NOT a safety net against a slicer, and a profile that emits more than the machine should run is a safety defect rather than an optimistic setting.
limits._note: These are stock motion limits. If your printer uses lower limits, install with --accel-cap matching your configured maximum.

tiers._semantics: Standard IS the stock Sovol profile — the baseline the machine ships with, renamed once it became clear how coarse it is. Draft IS Sovol's own speedBenchy. Optimal sits between Standard and Fine. Fine runs the other way entirely, taking the community's quality recommendations. Naming follows Voron/Prusa convention rather than the Draft of v1.0.2. Stock is a separate reference tier, faithful to Sovol's published profile and deliberately exempt from the ramp; it may end up hidden or personal rather than published.

Fine.derivation: extrapolate away from Draft past Standard — slower, more shells, artefact removal. Community quality recommendations, not interpolation.

Standard.derivation: verbatim Sovol stock Orca profile (0.20mm Standard @ 0.4 nozzle)

Draft.derivation: verbatim Sovol speedBenchy (8m22s). Expected to look bad; must not fail.
Draft._anchor_caveat: speedBenchy was gcode + 3MF, not a released profile. Its parameters were reverse-read from the 3MF and were never meant to compose with the stock filament profiles.

Stock.derivation: Verbatim Sovol published values, mapped through source/keymap.json. Reference/provenance tier, NOT part of the ramp.
Stock._note: Kept faithful rather than made consistent. It is the thing everything else is measured against, so 'fixing' it would destroy its only value. Expect it to violate the proportional model: stock asks outer 350 / inner 400 / infill 500 with no coherent ratio between them.

tiers._naming: Rungs are OrcaSlicer's Voron V0 ladder -- Extra Fine, Fine, Optimal, Standard, Draft, Extra Draft -- because the V0 is the closest analog to this machine and it is the vocabulary its users already read. Four are shipped; Extra Fine and Extra Draft are reserved for the ends. Renamed from Quality/Normal/Draft/Speed on 2026-09-02; v1.0.2's own 'ExtraDraft' came from this same ladder, so this is a return rather than a new scheme. SPEEDS STILL RAMP PER TIER, which is PrusaSlicer's Voron behaviour and not OrcaSlicer's -- Orca's Voron tiers differ in layer height alone. See docs/CEILINGS.md and docs/CONTEXTS.md.
tiers._variants_semantics: A SECOND AXIS, not a fifth rung. A tier trades quality against time inside a fixed envelope, and _order is checked as a monotonic ramp because of it. A variant sits ON one rung -- same nozzle, same layer height -- and spends material and time on mechanical properties instead. It is deliberately excluded from the ramp checks: it would tie with its anchor on the volumetric column and mean nothing there. See docs/CONTEXTS.md for the third axis, which is the machine envelope rather than either of these.

Strength.derivation: Standard's rung and layer height, Optimal's motion envelope, and a heavier shell. Walls hold ~2.4 mm of wall thickness rather than a wall COUNT, which is what lets one rule serve five nozzles: 6 loops at 0.4 and 4 at 0.6 is Bambu's own ladder (0.20mm/0.30mm Strength @BBL X1C) and it holds 2.52 mm both times, so the constant they are really keeping is thickness. Infill 10%% -> 25%% is unanimous across every vendor Strength profile shipped in OrcaSlicer 2.4.2; only Creality disagrees, upward, at 30%%.
Strength._why_slower: PrusaSlicer's STRUCTURAL is the other camp entirely: same geometry as its peers, 45-55%% of their speed and acceleration (0.20mm STRUCTURAL @MK4IS 0.4 runs perimeter 80 against SPEED's 170). Orca's vendors spend geometry; Prusa spends time. Both are cheap here, so this variant takes both -- flow_utilisation 0.7, which is Optimal's, against Standard's 1.0.
Strength._unmeasured: The ORDERING of the three effects -- walls, infill, dwell -- is not measured on this machine, and the chamber this pack already owns is very likely to outweigh all three for layer adhesion. Nothing here is a strength measurement; it is the consensus of what other vendors ship, applied through this pack's own model.
Strength._what_the_delta_is: Four keys against *SV Zero General*: perimeters (per NOZZLE, in the leaf, because what is held constant is 2.4 mm of wall), fill_density 10% -> 25%, top_solid_layers 4 -> 5, bottom_solid_layers 3 -> 4. All four are in source/keymap.json, so all three emitters promise the same thing. fill_pattern stays grid -- General already sets it, and grid is what Artillery and Creality switch TO for their own Strength profiles. ensure_vertical_shell_thickness is deliberately absent: the keymap has no Orca mapping for it and the value vocabularies differ (bool vs enum), so it would survive two emitters out of three.

Precision.derivation: Precision mode (klipper/modes/svzero-mode-precision.cfg): 2 mm3/s through the normal ratios, Prusa Core One 0.25 DETAIL accelerations, outer walls capped at 45 mm/s. A tier of the precision printer only; never offered on a standard one.
Precision._sqv_why: 1 mm/s (operator, 2026-10-14): precision is the slow fine-detail mode, so corners are taken at the lowest square corner velocity of any tier. It was 3, the same as Fine.

_sqv_note: SQUARE CORNER VELOCITY (SCV), per tier, in mm/s. Emitted explicitly to every slicer since 2026-10-05; before that it was declared here and emitted NOWHERE -- the 'passed to START_PRINT' path this note used to describe was never built, so every job ran printer.cfg's 5.0. How each slicer carries it (tools/generate.py apply_scv and emit_orca): PrusaSlicer, SuperSlicer and PS3 put 'SVZERO_SCV=<v>mm' in the print preset's Notes and a generated start G-code block turns it into SET_VELOCITY_LIMIT SQUARE_CORNER_VELOCITY -- a print-scope key all three define, unlike print_custom_variables, which is what broke PrusaSlicer in v1.0.2. OrcaSlicer gets its native per-feature jerk fields, all set to the tier value; measured 2026-10-05 on Orca 2.4.2 Klipper flavour, it emits nothing while default_jerk is 0 and clamps every value to machine_max_jerk_x, so the machine ceiling is raised to the highest tier. END_PRINT and CANCEL_PRINT restore printer.cfg's value. VALUES: Standard is stock, and stock is 5 (Sovol's Zero process sets every jerk to 5 and printer.cfg says 5.0), so Standard moved 7 -> 5 and Optimal 5 -> 4 to keep the ladder monotonic. Sovol's speedBenchy declares jerk 20 but default_jerk 0, so it never emitted them and ran at 5; Draft keeps 9 as the fast end. References for scale, from OrcaSlicer's vendor profiles with inheritance resolved inside each vendor (corrected 2026-10-05; an earlier reading resolved shared parents across vendors): Voron and Creality K2 set default 9 with outer wall 7; Snapmaker sets default 0 (off) with outer 2; Bambu, Qidi, Sovol SV08 and Sovol's own Zero profile leave default_jerk unset, so Orca sends nothing and the printer's configured value applies. Still PROPOSED, not measured on a Zero. Stock stays null: Sovol's stock profile emits no SCV, so neither does the reference.

layer_heights._note: Explicit rather than computed from layer_fraction, because the ladder is a design choice per nozzle and 0.2n deliberately breaks proportional scaling. Values are the existing SuperSlicer ladder, which is correct under Standard = stock: 0.4n Standard = 0.20 = stock's only process.
layer_heights._note_small_nozzles: 0.25 and 0.3 added 2026-10-05 (operator). Same shape as the 0.2 ladder -- 25 / 50 / 75% of the bore -- snapped to whole Z full steps (0.02 mm: 4 mm lead, 200 steps), so no layer ends mid-step: 0.25 -> 0.06 / 0.12 / 0.18, 0.3 -> 0.08 / 0.16 / 0.22. For scale, Prusa's Core One 0.25 runs 0.05/0.07/0.12/0.15 and its 0.3 runs 0.12/0.16/0.20.
layer_heights._note_precision: Precision on the small nozzles added 2026-10-14 (operator: 0.4 and below). The 0.4's band is 10-30% of the bore (0.04-0.12); the same band on whole Z full steps, floored at the precision printer's 0.04 minimum layer, gives 0.04/0.06 on the 0.2 and 0.25 and 0.04/0.06/0.08 on the 0.3.

tier_gaps._why: Deliberate omissions, asserted by tools/validate-bundle.py so they cannot be mistaken for oversights.
tier_gaps._why_no_02_strength: A 0.2 mm nozzle is a detail nozzle and holding 2.4 mm of wall there costs 12 loops. No vendor in OrcaSlicer 2.4.2 ships a 0.2-nozzle Strength profile either -- BBL, Creality and Artillery all start at 0.4.

_deferred: Filament volumetric caps, per-tier speed ceilings and the (process, filament-assumption) pairing are deliberately NOT modelled yet. Recorded in docs/STATUS.md: both published anchors already ask for speeds their own filament forbids (stock 350/400/500 against a 262 mm/s ceiling; speedBenchy 500 against 400). Revisit before publishing any tier that advertises a speed.

speed_model._why: Every tier speed is a ratio of one number per tier, so the ramp is driven by `base_speed` alone and cannot go backwards or drift out of proportion. The ratios were derived from the existing Fine/Optimal/Draft bases, which already agreed to within rounding: perimeter 45/66, 52/76, 69/100 = 68%; gap 59%; bridge 50%; first layer 10.5%. Standard disagreed on every row and is corrected.
speed_model._reference_chain: SuperSlicer resolves these against each other, not all against base_speed: external is a % of perimeter, solid a % of infill, top a % of solid. See PCT_REFERENCE in tools/generate.py.
speed_model._base_speed_note: Standard was 60 — below Optimal's 76 — which is what made infill run backwards. 88 places it evenly between Optimal and Draft. This is an interim value: Standard is defined as stock Sovol, whose real speeds are outer 350 / inner 400 / infill 500, and should be derived from the anchor once filament caps are settled.
speed_model._base_speed_strength_note: Optimal's number, not Standard's, because Strength deliberately gives back the speed Standard takes. Only reaches the tier BASE; every concrete preset's default_speed is derived from its own geometry by the flow model below.
speed_model._internal_bridge_note: Internal bridges at 150% of bridge_speed, the default of both SuperSlicer and OrcaSlicer, which define the percentage the same way. Until 2026-10-05 the tiers carried 400-402%: Sovol's stock 200 internal over 50 bridge, kept as a ratio after our bridge_speed became 50% of base -- so internal bridges asked for twice the tier's base speed and SuperSlicer's volumetric limiter set the real speed (21 mm3/s through a nozzle-diameter round strand: 668.5 mm/s on 0.2, 167.1 on 0.4), while Orca, never given the key, ran its own 150%.

_flow_design._answer: We are not the first: PrusaSlicer models exactly this split and has since long before us. Print settings -> Speed -> Max volumetric speed is documented as the hotend's capability; Filament settings -> Advanced -> Max volumetric speed is the material's; the lower of the two wins, and 0 disables that one. So the tidy separation exists.
_flow_design._the_real_untidiness: The machine limit lives in the PROCESS profile, not the printer profile. That is genuinely misplaced -- it must be repeated in every process, and setting it to 0 to 'not bother' silently disables the machine ceiling. Tom's Print Garden's bundle has max_volumetric_speed = 0 in its only process, which is also what produced the F0 start-gcode bug sebastianha traced. Orca is worse: no process-level field at all.
_flow_design._consequence_for_draft: Standard does NOT need hand-capping. The clamp is applied per feature by the slicer: features already under the ceiling are untouched, and only those exceeding it are slowed. So authoring Standard at stock's speeds with an honest volumetric pair produces exactly the requested behaviour -- the fastest extrusion type lands on the ceiling, everything else keeps its proportion. tomb16_ (Discord, 2024-10-21): 'Orca is smart enough to not exceed the flow rate so it will cap the speed... No problems are caused by hitting this limit.'

flow_model._why: A tier's speeds cannot be a single set of numbers, because volumetric demand is speed x line width x layer height and both width and layer scale with nozzle. At one infill speed the demand runs 7.9 mm3/s on a 0.2 nozzle and 157 on a 1.0. So the TIER carries ratios and each PRESET carries a default_speed derived from its own geometry.
flow_model._why_not_clamping: Letting the slicer clamp does not preserve feature ratios -- it inverts them. At stock's speeds against a 21 mm3/s ceiling, outer wall clamps to 262.5 and infill to 233.3, so the outer wall ends up FASTER than infill because infill's wider line hits the ceiling first. Scaling preserves the ordering; clamping destroys it. This corrects an earlier claim that Standard needed no hand-capping.
flow_model._formula: default_speed = (reference_flow * flow_utilisation) / (infill_width_ratio * nozzle * layer_height), capped by speed_cap.
flow_model._speed_cap_note: Stock's own sparse_infill_speed. Using Sovol's highest authored speed as the motion ceiling rather than inventing one. It binds on small nozzles, where flow is not the constraint: holding 21 mm3/s on a 0.2 nozzle would need 622 mm/s. Small nozzles are motion- and quality-limited, big ones flow-limited.

reference_flow._what: Filament capability each tier is authored against. A tier is a (process, reference_flow) pair; the speeds are meaningless without it.

flow_model._reference_flow_note: 21 is Sovol's own stock PLA filament profile -- what ships and what most people will run. 50 is the machine rating and what speedBenchy's filament profile declares, which is why Draft is authored against it. Re-author against a measured value once a flow test on a documented spool exists; known and trusted beats maximal.
flow_model._why_utilisation: Holding volumetric constant across tiers inverts the ramp: at a fixed flow, a thin layer needs MORE speed, so Fine came out fastest. Tiers must differ in how much of the available flow they use, not in the flow itself. Standard = 100% because Standard is stock capped at the ceiling, which is the stated definition; Fine and Optimal deliberately leave headroom, which is what buys surface finish.

_reference_flow_provenance.21: Sovol's stock PLA filament profile. NOT a Zero measurement: the same 21 appears on the classic SV08 and the SV08 MAX, whose toolheads differ from each other and from the Zero's. It is a house default carried along the product line, and it contradicts Sovol's own published rating for the Zero of <=50 mm3/s by 2.4x. See notes/kb/toolhead-lineage.md.
_reference_flow_provenance.50: Sovol's published machine rating, and the value the speedBenchy 3MF declares. WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS: the 8m22s speedBenchy was released as gcode and a 3MF, never as a profile, so it was never intended to pair with a stock filament profile. It is a demo artefact, tuned as a whole for one model on one filament. Treat it as evidence that 50 is reachable, not as a profile to interpolate against.
_reference_flow_provenance._action: Both anchors are weak for different reasons. A flow test on a documented spool replaces both and rescales the entire ladder from one number.
_reference_flow_provenance._sv08_community_floor: The SV08 community has measured flow; the Zero's has not. On a STOCK 0.4 hotend: rappetor 24 mm3/s (PLA+), zappes.bpd 30 (Sunlu PETG), skaltura 36. Exclude upgraded hotends (Dragon, CHT, OXC) which range 19-70 and measure a different part. The SV08's heater is 64-72W against the Zero's 85W, so these are a FLOOR for the Zero, not a match. Range narrows from [21,50] to roughly [24,50]. Note promptengineered raised 18->25 mm3/s by increasing extruder motor current to 0.9A, so a flow test measures the whole path, not the hotend.

targets._why: Which slicer schema each emitter is known-good against. Real PrusaSlicer bundles stamp '# generated by PrusaSlicer <ver>' on line 1; ours declared nothing, so a schema change would be discovered by a confusing import failure rather than by a version mismatch. Stamped into the generated headers. Versions verified from the GitHub releases API on 2026-09-01, not from memory.

superslicer.status: EMITTED ONLY, no longer the master. Last release 2025-11-19 and it is a PRERELEASE -- the 2.7.61.x before it are prereleases too, so there is no recent stable at all. Not on Flathub and not in Fedora's repos; installed 2026-09-01 from the upstream linux64 tarball at ~/opt/superslicer-2.7.62.0 (self-contained, no missing libs on glibc 2.43, no sudo), reachable as `tools/sandbox.sh superslicer`. Before that it had never been installed here, so the bundle was never round-tripped through its own application.

prusaslicer.status: verified installed (flatpak). 90/90 print keys shared with the emitted SuperSlicer bundle.

orcaslicer.status: verified installed (flatpak), released 2026-07-07 after 2.4.0 and 2.4.1 in the same month -- the only one of the three shipping stables. 13/90 keys shared, translated via source/keymap.json.

prusaslicer_3.status: public alpha 2026-09-01. Profiles are YAML fragments; the schema is vendored at source/ps3/preset-schema.json and enforced against source/presets.json on every run. NOT emitted: third-party vendors are deferred upstream, so an emitter could be written but not tested. The key space survived -- of 158 keys in Prusa's own 3.0 print presets only 5 are new to 2.9.6. See docs/PIPELINE.md.

small_nozzles._why: Rules for every nozzle below 0.4, adopted by the operator on 2026-10-05: a first layer at 80% of the bore (Prusa's own ratio on its Core One 0.25, which runs a 0.2 first layer) and 3 walls (Core One 0.25 runs 3; Bambu, Qidi and Creality run 4 on a 0.2). The motion anchor -- Sovol SV08's 0.2 wall speed and accelerations -- was adopted for the 0.2 and extended to 0.25 and 0.3: below 0.4 the flow model asks for more than the 500 mm/s motion cap at fine layers, which is what put 0.2 walls at 340/282 before. The anchor's cap is its inner-wall speed over our perimeter ratio, so every other feature keeps its proportion; where the flow model asks for less, flow still binds.

motion_anchor._source: Sovol SV08 0.2 nozzle, 0.10mm Standard: inner wall 200, outer 160, default/outer/inner acceleration 20000/8000/12000 (archived Sovol-OrcaSlicer profiles f1d3dca). With our 83% outer ratio the outer wall lands at 166.
motion_anchor._accel_note: Every acceleration the SV08 0.2 preset sets, written absolute into each small-nozzle preset so no tier ratio leaks in: default 20000, inner 12000, outer 8000, top 12000, first layer 3000; sparse and solid infill unset there, so Orca's default applies (20000); bridges 100% of the outer wall in Orca's dialect (8000).

small_nozzles._modes: The motion anchor is for the standard printer's tiers. A machine mode's tier keeps its own accelerations, which on precision are Prusa Core One 0.25 DETAIL's under a 4000 mm/s^2 ceiling; the SV08 0.2 anchor's 20000 would exceed what the mode file allows. The first layer and wall rules apply to every tier.

accel_model._why: Option B of notes/acceleration-tiers-2026-10-05.md, chosen by the operator 2026-10-06: keep the tier ramp, re-anchor it. Targets are absolute mm/s2 per feature. apply_accel_model writes them into the SuperSlicer-native master in its own relative form -- default and inner wall absolute, every other feature as a percentage of its chain base (ACCEL_REFERENCE) -- so SuperSlicer stays relative and PrusaSlicer/Orca resolve back to these exact numbers. check() refuses any feature that goes backwards along the ramp. Travel stays on its own 5000 policy.

Fine._anchor: Prusa Core One 0.4 STRUCTURAL (PrusaResearch.ini, PrusaSlicer 2.9.6) scaled by 2/3 so its 6000 infill peak is 4000 (operator, 2026-10-14); every feature keeps its proportion. First layer 261 rather than 333: the scaled value went above Optimal's, and the ladder may not go backwards. Travel 4000, the same ceiling.

Optimal._anchor: Scaled by 6000/11500 so the 11500 infill peak is 6000, the Y axis's measured shaper limit (Zero2 MZV sweep, notes/kb/input-shaping.md; operator, 2026-10-14); every feature keeps its proportion. Top 1438 rather than 1565: the scaled value went above Standard's, and the ladder may not go backwards. Was 10000 default and 11500 infill, the X limit.

Standard._anchor: Sovol's stock Zero process scaled by 11500/40000 so its 40000 peak is 11500, the X axis's measured shaper limit (operator, 2026-10-14); every feature keeps stock's proportions. Standard was stock verbatim until then.

Draft._anchor: Just above stock: the outer wall at the X recommendation (11500), the inner wall in stock's 83.3% proportion, everything else at stock. Sovol's speedBenchy itself asks 40000 on every wall; that lives on as the hidden speedboat reference, not as a published tier.

Precision._anchor: Prusa Core One 0.25 DETAIL (operator, 2026-10-05) scaled by 2/3 so its 3000 peak is 2000 (operator, 2026-10-14); every feature keeps its proportion. Travel 2000, the same ceiling. The mode file's 4000 ceiling is unchanged, so it is headroom.

accel_model._why_2026_10_14: Re-anchored on the Zero's measured input-shaper limits (operator, 2026-10-14): each tier is scaled as a whole so its peak is Precision 2000, Fine 4000, Optimal 6000 (Y), Standard 11500 (X), every feature keeping its proportion to the others. Draft keeps stock's 40000 as the fast end; Strength follows Optimal. Where scaling sent the ladder backwards the earlier tier takes the later one's value (Fine first layer, Optimal top). Travel is per tier, at most the peak. Small nozzles' SV08 0.2 accelerations are scaled the same way so their peak is the tier's.

modes._why: A machine mode is a Klipper configuration selected by a mode file and a restart: precision runs X/Y at 64 microsteps, 2.4 A, under a 300 mm/s and 4000 mm/s^2 ceiling. Its tiers belong to a printer of their own, whose start G-code names the mode in SVZERO_REQUIRE, so the handshake refuses a job sliced for the other mode. Standard mode is every printer not listed here.

precision._nozzles_why: 0.4 and below (operator, 2026-10-14), every nozzle the pack ships under the 0.4. It was 0.4 only from 2026-10-05, because a nozzle swap is a hardware modification on the Zero; the small nozzles were added to the standard printer the same day, and fine detail is what both are for.
precision._default_layer_why: Orca's default print profile for each precision machine: 0.08, or the nozzle's thickest precision layer where 0.08 is outside its band (0.06 on the 0.2 and 0.25).
precision._flow_reference_why: The tier's 2 mm3/s is the 0.4's. On a smaller nozzle it scales with the bore, so each layer height runs the 0.4's speeds: held at 2 mm3/s, the 0.2 at 0.04 would ask 151 mm/s of its inner walls against the 0.4's 76, which is not a slow, quiet mode (2026-10-14, with the small-nozzle precision printers).
precision._machine_why: The ceiling svzero-mode-precision.cfg enforces: 300 mm/s is the step-rate budget at 64 microsteps (5 x microsteps x v x sqrt 2 steps/s at stock's 1200 mm/s and 16), 4000 the highest acceleration any precision tier asks for. The minimum layer, 0.04, is authored on the printer in source/presets.json.
precision._outer_wall_cap_why: Prusa Core One 0.25 DETAIL's outer wall speed (operator, 2026-10-05). Binds only at 0.04 mm.
precision._exclude_why: TPU is the expected exclusion (operator, 2026-10-05): a flexible filament at 64 microsteps and a 2 mm3/s budget gains nothing and buckles in the extruder.
